biological.citation: Regulation of cortical neurogenesis by MED13L via transcriptional priming and its implications for MED13L syndrome (PMID: 40775066)
biological.summary: Homozygous Med13l knockout mice show neonatal lethality with reduced brain volume and cortical thickness, while heterozygous mice display impaired learning/memory, reduced motor coordination, and microcephaly. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed severe cortical neurogenesis deficits driven by impaired neural progenitor differentiation. Multi-omics analyses showed MED13L orchestrates cortical neurogenesis by priming transcriptional activation of key developmental genes (Neurod2, Sox5, Auts2, Nfib) through binding to the core Mediator complex, facilitating RNA Pol II association.

biological.citation: Impaired development of neural-crest cell-derived organs and intellectual disability caused by MED13L haploinsufficiency (PMID: 25137640)
biological.summary: Knockdown of the MED13L zebrafish orthologue med13b caused early defective migration of cranial neural crest cells, contributing to cartilage structure deformities and abnormal distribution of developing neurons in different brain regions, which was rescued by introduction of full-length human MED13L mRNA. In ES-derived human neural progenitors, MED13L knockdown followed by neuronal differentiation revealed differential expression of Wnt and FGF signaling pathway components by transcriptome analysis.

biological.citation: MED13L integrates Mediator-regulated epigenetic control into lung cancer radiosensitivity (PMID: 32802198)
biological.summary: Radiation triggers disassembly of the Mediator complex via miR-4497-mediated silencing of MED13L in NSCLC cells. Suppression of MED13L attenuated physical interactions between the core Mediator and CDK8 kinase module, reduced recruitment of acetyltransferase P300 to chromatin, diminished global H3K27ac signals, and decreased expression of multiple oncogenes including PRKCA. Inhibition of PRKCA potentiated radiotherapy killing effects in vitro and in vivo xenograft models.

biological.citation: The SCF-Fbw7 ubiquitin ligase degrades MED13 and MED13L and regulates CDK8 module association with Mediator (PMID: 23322298)
biological.summary: Fbw7, a tumor suppressor and ubiquitin ligase, binds to CDK8-Mediator and targets MED13/MED13L for proteasomal degradation. MED13/MED13L physically link the CDK8 kinase module to the core Mediator complex, and loss of Fbw7 increases CDK8 module-Mediator association. This reveals a novel post-translational mechanism regulating CDK8 module-Mediator dynamics.

biological.citation: Aberrant cyclin C nuclear release induces mitochondrial fragmentation and dysfunction in MED13L syndrome fibroblasts (PMID: 35198885)
biological.summary: Patient fibroblasts harboring the MED13L S1497F/fs allele exhibited aberrant cytoplasmic cyclin C localization, mitochondrial fragmentation, a 6-fold reduction in respiration, reduced mtDNA copy number, and hypersensitivity to oxidative stress. MED13L normally tethers the cyclin C-CDK8 kinase module to the Mediator complex, and its loss allows cyclin C to mis-localize to mitochondria and drive fragmentation. Pharmacological or genetic prevention of cyclin C-mitochondrial localization corrected the fragmented mitochondrial phenotype and partially restored organelle function.

biological.citation: Expression Analyses of Mediator Complex Subunit 13-Like: A Responsible Gene for Neurodevelopmental Disorders during Mouse Brain Development (PMID: 33794529)
biological.summary: MED13L exhibits tissue-dependent and developmental stage-dependent expression in mouse brain, with relatively high expression in the ventricular zone of the cerebral cortex at embryonic day 14 and diffuse cytoplasmic distribution throughout the cortex by postnatal day 30. MED13L partially colocalizes with pre- and post-synaptic markers (synaptophysin and PSD95) in primary cultured hippocampal neurons, suggesting a role in synaptic function. Expression is also cell type- and developmental stage-specific in the hippocampus and cerebellum.

biological.citation: MED13L and its disease-associated variants influence the dendritic development of cerebral cortical neurons in the mammalian brain (PMID: 36798993)
biological.summary: In utero electroporation of mouse cortical neurons showed that disease-associated MED13L missense variants (p.P866L, p.T2162M, p.S2163L, p.S2177Y) differ in subcellular localization, with some accumulating in the nucleus and others in the cytoplasm. mMED13L knockdown abrogated dendritic growth in vivo, rescued by RNAi-resistant MED13L but not by p.S2163L variant; overexpression of p.P866L reduced dendrite number and length in cortical layer II/III pyramidal neurons. None of the variants affected neuronal migration or callosal axon elongation, indicating MED13L specifically regulates dendritic branching in cortical excitatory neurons.

biological.citation: Med13 and Med13L: Critical redundant players in basal cardiac function and gene expression (PMID: 40989238)
biological.summary: Inducible cardiomyocyte-specific double knockout of Med13 and Med13L in adult mice resulted in lethal heart failure within a median of 6 weeks, demonstrating their partially redundant roles in maintaining basal cardiac function. RNAseq revealed significant gene dysregulation including fibrotic pathways and calcium handling genes, with similar patterns observed across other Mediator cardiac knockouts (Med12, Med1, Med30). Med13 and Med13L are mutually exclusive paralogs within the kinase submodule of the Mediator complex.

biological.citation: Depletion of Mediator Kinase Module Subunits Represses Superenhancer-Associated Genes in Colon Cancer Cells (PMID: 29507187)
biological.summary: Depletion of MED13 together with MED13L in colon cancer cells caused a disproportional decrease in expression of cancer-acquired superenhancer-associated genes, including MYC, with a concomitant decrease in cell proliferation. MED12-MED13/MED13L-dependent superenhancer genes were co-regulated by β-catenin, which associates with MED12, and β-catenin depletion reduced MED12 binding at the MYC superenhancer. This effect was distinct from CDK8/CDK19 depletion, implicating MED13/MED13L as structural rather than kinase-dependent regulators of superenhancer activity.

biological.citation: ASHG 2025 - MED13L knockout in cerebral organoids leads to a shifted developmental program through abnormal cis-regulatory element activation (ASHG 2023 - J. Ghoumid et al.)
biological.summary: MED13L knockout cerebral organoids derived from human iPSCs produced only neuroretinal cells instead of cortical neurons, demonstrating a fundamental shift in developmental program. Single-cell RNAseq and scATAC-seq revealed coordinated activation of neuroretinal-specific OTX2 and PAX6 cis-regulatory elements (CREs) in knockout organoids, while forebrain-specific CREs (AN1, AN2) were not activated. These findings indicate MED13L is critical for proper enhancer activation during neural induction, and its loss leads to global neural gene expression misregulation.
